TheDeclineoftheOttomanEmpire
There were many factors behind the decline of the OttomanEmpire, but the most
prominent ones are as follows:
The internal socio-economic weakness of the ottoman Empire encouraged the
Europeans to gain theirlost lands from the Ottomans.
When the able and wise viziers lost their powers, the incompetent rulers and
officials schemed to influence the Imperial Family to govern the Empire with
methods based on briberyand nepotism.
After Suleyman the Magnificent, appointments to official positions remained no
more based on merit, rather it started to be based on political intrigues.
The Janissaries (the Ottoman land forces) became highly politicized and outdated,
and refusedto change.
The sultans who wanted to modernize the Empire's institutions faced opposition
from influential old groups and clerics,and they were even assassinated just like in
thecasesofOsman Il andSelimIl.
Economic difficulties started in the late 16th century, with the closure of
international trade routes by the British and the Portuguese.This resulted in the
decline of prosperity of the Middle Eastern provinces and caused inflation in the
Ottoman economy.This inflation weakenedthetraditional industries and trade.
While the Europeans adopted modern technology with the Industrial Revolution, the
Ottomans were left far behind due to slow response and constant internal conflicts.
Reform attempts in the Ottoman Empire could not achieve lasting results. Eventually in
April 1909, a group of young military officers who labelled themselves as ‘Young Turks'
invaded Istanbul and launched a coup against Sultan Abdulhamid l to dethrone him.
